To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a morphing wing leading edge can be designed and manufactured with low cost and that the morphing wing leading-edge prototype is able to modify the stall angle of a wing.
we have developed and tested a morphing leading-edge system that is simple to manufacture, light in weight, and that modifies the stall angle of a wing.
a morphing leading-edge concept for a medium unmanned aircraft has been successfully tested in the wind tunnel, with a stall angle of 20° and a slope of lift coefficient of 0.05.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a morphing leading-edge system that can modify the shape of the wing to increase the maximum stall angle and, therefore, increase the maximum lift coefficient of the wing.
the design of a wing with a morphing leading-edge system that can increase the stall angle without changing the slope of the curve lift coefficient.
the design of a new concept for a morphing leading-edge for an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) wing.

this paper presents the design, manufacturing and testing of a new concept for morphing leading edge using a subsonic blow down wind tunnel.
a morphing leading-edge system is a feasible and viable solution to improve the aerodynamic performance of a wing in the stall regime.
the results presented here are promising for the design of a wing including morphing leading edge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we designed and manufactured a new concept for a morphing leading-edge using a subsonic blow down wind tunnel, which can increase the stall angle and the lift of the wing.
this paper is the first to show the possibility of modifying stall angles of a wing using a morphing cambers system.
the concept of the morphing camber is a promising concept for the design of a wing with a morphing leading-edge.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of a new concept for a morphing leading-edge system is feasible, but that further optimization work is needed to increase the deformation of the leading-edge and, thus, the increase in the stall angle of a wing with a morphing leading-edged system.
the concept of the morphing camber is feasible, even with simple and light structures, which makes it suitable for UAVs.
a morphing leading edges can be designed to improve the performance of an aircraft in terms of lift and drag.
